Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB, Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Johnson, Head of Investor Relations.

Alex Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s Q3 FY2024 results. With me on the call are Mike Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Marketing Officer; David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer; Emma Lopez, Chief Innovation Officer; Tom Reynolds, Chief Sales Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mike Rivera.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities.

Our discussion today will cover eight key aspects: summary of financial results and outlook; performance by key categories and brands; geographic performance in developed versus emerging markets; key strategic priorities and progress; supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings impact; price elasticity observations; competitive activity and response; and marketing campaign effectiveness.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $15.8 billion, representing a 6% increase on a reported basis and 5% on an organic basis compared to the prior year. Gross margin was 53.2%, driven by supply chain efficiencies, favorable commodity hedging, and mix benefits from premium products. Operating income was $3.5 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.32. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining our Q3 FY2024 earnings call for Global Consumer Brands. Today, I'll walk you through our financial results, which once again demonstrate the resilience and execution power of our CPG portfolio amid a dynamic macroeconomic environment. We'll then share our outlook, which reflects growing confidence in our strategy to drive sustainable, profitable growth.

Starting with the headline numbers: For the third quarter, we delivered net revenues of $15.8 billion, up 6% on a reported basis and 5% on an organic basis. Organic growth broke down to 1% volume growth and 4% pricing, a healthy mix that underscores our pricing discipline while protecting consumer value through targeted promotions and loyalty programs. Adjusted diluted EPS came in at $1.32, up 12% year-over-year, beating our guidance midpoint and reflecting strong operating leverage.

Gross margins expanded 250 basis points to 53.2%, driven by a combination of supply chain efficiencies, favorable commodity hedging, and mix benefits from premium products. Core operating expenses grew only 3%, below revenue growth, leading to an adjusted operating margin of 22.1%, up 180 basis points. Free cash flow was robust at $2.1 billion, supporting $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a quarterly dividend of $0.48 per share, up 5% from last year. Our net leverage ratio stands at a healthy 2.1x, giving us ample dry powder for strategic M&A.

Diving into geographic performance, which continues to underscore the resilience and growth potential of our diversified portfolio across developed and emerging markets. In Q3 FY2024, total net sales reached $15.8 billion, up 6% as reported and 5% on an organic basis, with pricing contributing 4 points and volume/mix 1 point globally.

Developed markets—North America, Western Europe, and Australia/New Zealand—represent approximately 60% of our revenue base and grew organic sales 2%, a sequential improvement driven by disciplined pricing and premiumization amid persistent inflation pressures. North America, our largest market at 45% of total sales, delivered 5% organic growth on market share gains in 9 of our top 10 categories. Premium snacks like our NutriBoost bar line gained 2.2 points of market share per IRI data. In Western Europe, we faced a 1% organic decline, primarily volume softness in mass-market fabric care due to downtrading and high energy costs, but pricing actions of +5% helped mitigate this.

Emerging markets, representing 40% of revenue, saw explosive 12% organic growth—more than double the developed market rate. Asia-Pacific led with 15% growth, excluding FX, powered by 10% volume expansion in India and Southeast Asia. In India, our DailyEssentials sachet packs in beauty and personal care grew 18%. Latin America delivered 11% organic growth despite FX headwinds, led by Brazil's 13% volume surge in beverages and snacks. Africa/Middle East rounded out at 10% growth.

Key trends shaping this include structural tailwinds in emerging markets like a rising middle class and e-commerce explosion. We're allocating 65% of our $1.2 billion FY2024 CapEx to emerging markets, focusing on supply chain localization, digital acceleration, and portfolio optimization. Looking forward, we expect developed markets to stabilize at 3-4% organic growth in the second half, while emerging accelerates to mid-teens.

Before segment details, a few words on price elasticity observations, which have been a key driver of our Q3 performance. Our observed price elasticity across the portfolio improved to -0.45 in Q3, up from -0.65 in the year-ago quarter and better than the category average of -0.55 per NielsenIQ. We executed targeted ASP hikes averaging 3.2% year-over-year, contributing 450 basis points to organic sales growth, while unit volumes declined just 1.4%.

By segment: Beauty & Personal Care at -0.35, Household Essentials at -0.50, Food & Beverage at -0.60. Regionally, North America strongest at -0.40, Europe more elastic at -0.65, emerging at -0.50. Our AI-powered pricing engine and Elasticity Optimizer tool enabled dynamic adjustments, predicting outcomes with 92% accuracy. This affirms our Value Over Volume strategy, with runway for another 2-3% pricing in FY24.

On competitive activity, the CPG sector remains fiercely contested, with private label penetration accelerating to 22%. We defended our positions despite aggressive pricing from P&G, Unilever, and PepsiCo. Our response included dynamic pricing via RGM platform, recapturing share in snacks; innovation launches like EcoShield and KetoFuel; and omnichannel expansion adding 5,200 PODs. Regionally, we gained in North America and EMEA via sustainability edges. Looking ahead, our agile supply chain and data analytics position us to outpace peers.

Strategically, we're sharpening our portfolio—we divested low-margin businesses for $450 million, redeploying into acquisitions like IndieBio. Challenges like inflation on cocoa persist, but offset by productivity.

Turning to outlook, we're raising full-year FY2024 guidance: organic sales growth of 4-5%, adjusted EPS $5.45-$5.55, gross margin expansion of 150-200 basis points. For Q4, organic growth of 3-4%, adjusted EPS $1.35-$1.40. These results validate our Thrive25 strategy.

With that, next Lisa Chen will provide insights on our marketing and brand initiatives.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Our brand building efforts have contributed significantly to our performance. We are seeing strong engagement across all our channels, especially with our new Refresh & Renew campaign.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into one of our key growth drivers: marketing campaign effectiveness. In the CPG space, battling competition from Procter & Gamble, Unilever, and private labels, our A&P discipline delivered 8% organic sales growth this quarter, outpacing the Nielsen category average of 3.2%.

We invested $485 million in A&P, up 12% year-over-year, representing 14% of net sales—in line with our 13-15% target. This yielded a blended ROAS of 4.7x, up 24% from 3.8x last year, above the 3.5x CPG benchmark, contributing $2.1 billion in incremental revenue. Our marketing efficiency score hit 2.8, up from 2.1.

By pillar, Refresh & Renew for NovaQuench hydration and SparkleFizz sodas generated 6.2x ROAS, with 15 million GRPs in North America, 28% uplift in penetration. Digital at 65% of spend drove 82% of lift via AI-powered DCO with The Trade Desk, boosting CTR 42% and cutting CPMs 18% to $12.50.

Digital now 58% of A&P mix, up from 45% two years ago. RMNs like Amazon DSP and Walmart Connect drove 35% of e-comm growth at 7.1x ROAS; CleanGlow on Amazon improved ACOS 22%. Social and influencers at 22% spend: TikTok for SnackAttack lifted AOV from $18 to $25, 14 million UGC impressions, 12% Gen Z trial.

Regionally: North America (52% sales) 9% lift, 1.2 share points; Europe (22%) 5.1x ROAS on GreenWave personal care; APAC 18% uplift, China WeChat 25% conversions; LATAM 8% lift on Copa América activations.

Technically, MMM with Bayesian stats and zero-party data from GCB Rewards (10M users) at 95% accuracy; incrementality tests show 27% digital incremental. DTC Shopify with Klaviyo hit 12x ROAS, CAC down 31% to $14.50, CLV up 18 months.

Our Precision Marketing 2.0—always-on branding plus agile activations—emphasizes purpose like net-zero packaging. Ahead, 20% more to CTV/DOOH, targeting 5.2x ROAS, generative AI for ads cutting costs 40%. This protects 22.4% EBITDA margins amid private label pressure.

In summary, marketing is accelerating top-line growth while optimizing P&L.

Following me, David Patel will discuss supply chain performance.

David Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to optimize our supply chain network and implement advanced technologies to improve efficiency and resilience. We are also focused on reducing our carbon footprint.

Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'd like to dive deep into the meaningful impact from supply chain efficiencies and productivity savings. These initiatives delivered approximately $285 million in run-rate savings year-over-year, contributing 120 basis points to gross margin expansion to 48.2%. This builds on $210 million in Q3 2023 from our SupplySync 2.0 program.

Savings offset 65% of 4.2% raw material inflation, like palm oil up 8% from El Niño. Supply chain costs declined 210 basis points sequentially. KPIs: inventory turns 8.2x (working capital down $420M), OTIF 96.5%, perfect order 94%.

Technical initiatives: AI/ML demand sensing across 85% SKUs reduced forecast error 28%, safety stock 12%; warehouse AGVs in 15 DCs boosted throughput 22%, labor 18%; blockchain traceability for 60% ingredients slashed disputes 40%; transportation optimization cut freight 14%.

Regionally: North America $140M from DC consolidation, e-comm fill 98%; EMEA $75M despite energy inflation, nearshoring pulp; APAC/LATAM $70M, India VMI cut obsolescence 30%.

These build resilience against shocks, Scope 3 down 12%. Reinvesting 40% into innovation for 5-7% topline uplift. FY24 incremental $350-400M savings, scaling to $500M by FY25.

After me, Emma Lopez will share updates on our product innovation pipeline.

Emma Lopez:
Thank you, David. We are excited about our pipeline of innovative products. Our recent product launch, Electrolyte Boost variant of AquaPure, has been well-received by consumers, driving 25% dollar sales growth.

Thank you, and good morning, everyone. I'll now dive into our performance by key categories and brands, where we delivered resilient growth amid a dynamic macro environment. Our portfolio across Beverages, Snacks & Confectionery, Beauty & Personal Care, and Home Care represents over 95% of our $18.7 billion trailing twelve-month revenue. We grew organic net sales 4.2% in Q3, outpacing global CPG average of 2.1% per NielsenIQ, with 2.8% volume/mix and 1.4% pricing—eighth straight quarter of volume growth.

Beverages (28% sales) grew 6.1%, volume/mix 4.2%. AquaPure alkaline water surged 12% penetration to 28% in North America, Electrolyte Boost (sustainable coconut water) drove 25% growth, e-comm up 40%. North America 7.5%, EMEA 5.2% share to 14.2%, APAC 3.1% offset by ZenLeaf 8% in India. 65% pipeline RTD functionals targeting $50B better-for-you segment.

Snacks & Confectionery (32%) 5.8% growth vs. industry 3.4%, all volume/mix. CrunchyBites baked snacks exploded 18%, #1 plant-based on Walmart.com, 35% repeats. LATAM 9.2%, SweetHarmony 1.5 points share in Brazil; Europe No Added Sugar gummies 14%. AI shelf optimization boosted distribution 3 points.

Beauty & Personal Care (22%) 3.5%, pricing 4.7%. GlowEssence 9% on Night Renew serum, 8% anti-aging share, DTC 25%. APAC 6.8% SilkWave on K-beauty; blockchain shea butter. Pruning SKUs, divesting deodorant for $150M to fund prestige M&A.

Home Care (23%) 2.9% vs. flat category. PureShield 7%, Probiotic Power 22% in Europe. North America 4.1% club channels; EMEA refill pilots cut plastic 40%; India 12% via Project Shakti.

Across, $450M YTD savings reinvested in 12 launches at 20%+ margins. E-comm 18%, share up 60 bps to 7.2%, premium 3x core. Confident in 4-5% organic FY growth.

Finally, Tom Reynolds will discuss our sales performance and channel strategy.

Tom Reynolds:
Thank you, Emma. We are focused on expanding our distribution channels and improving our sales execution. We are seeing strong growth in our e-commerce channel, now 22% of sales, and we are also investing in our retail partnerships.

As part of our key strategic priorities, our four-pillar strategy—Power Brands Acceleration, Innovation-Led Growth, Sustainability Imperative, and Digital & Operational Excellence—shows strong momentum. Our 15 power brands grew 9.2% organically, outpacing categories by 450 bps. CrispWave gained 120 bps to 28% share; PureGlow 12% growth.

Innovation: 18 launches, NutriBoost $45M sales, 3.5x ROI. R&D up 15% with precision fermentation.

Sustainability: Scope 1/2 down 22%, packaging 92% recyclable, sustainable SKUs +18%.

Digital: E-comm up to 22%, AI personalization +28% conversions; $280M savings, inventory turns 7.2x.

Regionally aligns: North America 7%, Europe 5%, APAC 16%, LATAM 11%. Raised FY guidance: 6-7% organic, EPS $4.85-$4.95.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. The question-and-answer session instructions. Our first question comes from Jennifer Lee with Morgan Stanley.

Jennifer Lee:
How is your company addressing the increasing demand for sustainable products?

Emma Lopez:
Great question, Jennifer. Sustainability is core to our innovation pipeline and categories performance. We've hit 92% packaging recyclability ahead of targets, with rPET bottles for EcoThirst reducing virgin plastic 30%. Probiotic Power cleaners leverage microbiome tech, 99.9% efficacy, resonating post-COVID. Scope 3 down 12% via regenerative ag, and sustainable SKUs grew 18% at premium prices. Our Responsible Sourcing covers 85% Tier 1 suppliers, appealing to 75% of millennials prioritizing ESG. This drives loyalty and share gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Goldman Sachs.

David Kim:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Tom Reynolds:
Thanks, David. Emerging markets are key, with 12% organic growth. We're allocating 65% CapEx there, localizing supply chains with new plants in India, Indonesia, Mexico—cutting lead times 30%. Digital investments like $150M in AI forecasting, plus 20+ emerging innovations like halal snacks. In APAC, India 25% via SpiceEssence, China 12%; LATAM Brazil 20% affordability packs. E-comm partnerships with Shopee, JioMart expanding rural penetration 16%. This drives mid-teens growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with JPMorgan.

Maria Gonzalez:
Can you discuss the impact of inflation on your pricing strategy and consumer demand?

Sarah Thompson:
Sure, Maria. Inflation lingers but peaking on commodities like cocoa. Our elasticity at -0.45 buffered 3.2% ASP hikes, volumes down just 1.4%. Pricing contributed 4 points to organic growth. AI pricing engine optimizes by segment/region, e.g., inelastic beauty -0.35 allows trade-up. We're shifting to EDLP, reducing TPRs, while reinvesting productivity savings. Consumer demand resilient in premium/health, with emerging markets offsetting developed softness.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Chen with Barclays.

Robert Chen:
How are you leveraging artificial intelligence to improve your supply chain efficiency?

David Patel:
Excellent point, Robert. AI/ML demand sensing across 85% SKUs integrates POS, weather, sentiment—forecast error down 28%, safety stock 12%. In warehouses, AGVs boost throughput 22%. Pricing uses AI elasticity heatmaps for ZIP-level adjustments. Marketing DCO tests 1,200 variants, CTR up 42%. Overall, $285M savings, turns 8.2x, positioning for FY25 $500M.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Mike Rivera for closing remarks.

Mike Rivera:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your insightful questions and participation. We are confident in our ability to deliver long-term sustainable growth and create value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Johnson:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
